VERDICT: CHALLENGE C0031 | `scan_health()` creates a fresh local `tools_available = {}` on every call, then iterates all four runners unconditionally. There is no persisted unavailable-tool cache across calls, and no intra-call prior state to consult before the loop. The proposed fix references “Skip tools already marked unavailable in tools_available”, but that dict is populated only after each runner returns/raises, so it cannot suppress any first invocation in the same scan and there is no remembered state for later scans. This is not a real bug in the current code.

VERDICT: CHALLENGE C0042 | The parser is intentionally documented to accept ASCII `->` forms (`"Line N: old -> new"`). `->` appearing inside Python code fragments is only ambiguous if the free-form fix text itself is underspecified; the current regex splits at the first separator after `Line N:` and still works for common single-line replacements. Replacing the protocol with Unicode `→` would break compatibility with likely model output and is not the simplest PoC fix.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0038 | Misclassifying all Ruff `F*` codes as `DEAD_CODE` also corrupts the advertised defect-detection feature downstream: `scan_health()` aggregates `counts_by_category` from these categories, so live-name/runtime-safety findings like `F821 undefined name` get reported as dead code in the endocrine health summary, misleading the insect brain’s health trend and any consumer of `health_trend()`.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` claims sandboxed fix verification but its post-fix static analysis is executed on the patched file path alone (`_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, patched_path)`, same for ruff/bandit). `run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, and `run_bandit` all accept a path list and are being invoked on a single file, not the mirrored sandbox project. For import-sensitive tools this means analysis scope is file-only even after `_create_sandbox()` mirrors sibling files. Evidence: the sandbox creator returns both `tmpdir` and `patched_path`, but only `patched_path` is ever analyzed; `tmpdir` is only used as `cwd` for optional tests.
FOLLOW: A fix that breaks other copied files, package-level imports, or cross-file type assumptions can still be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL because the tool pass never inspects the sandboxed project as a project. This undermines the core “does the proposed fix break anything?” capability and can mark harmful fixes as verified; immune stage 4 then sets `finding.verified = True`, enabling the bug-closed gate on a false premise in later rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — run pre/post tool baselines against the sandbox project scope, not the single patched file. After creating the sandbox, invoke each tool on the sandboxed source path set (or at minimum on the sandbox root/project-relative file set) with `cwd=tmpdir`, and compare like-for-like project-scope counts.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()`, `run_ruff()`, `run_bandit()`, and `run_mypy()` invoke binaries using absolute hard-coded macOS Python 3.13 paths under `/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/bin/...`. Unlike `immune_agents.py`, endocrine has no discovery/fallback logic. On any machine without that exact interpreter layout, health scan degrades to “tool missing” for every tool and fix evaluation loses its analyzers. Evidence: constants `PYRIGHT_BIN`, `RUFF_BIN`, `BANDIT_BIN`, `MYPY_BIN`, `PYTHON_313` are hard-coded from `_TOOL_BIN`; `scan_health()` just catches `ToolNotFoundError` and marks unavailable.
FOLLOW: End-to-end endocrine features silently fail on non-matching environments: health scan returns no diagnostics, tool availability becomes mostly false, fix evaluation baselines collapse, and pacing is the only live feature. Because this module is infrastructure meant to run between rounds, environment-coupled failure makes the layer non-portable and easy to ship in a nonfunctional state for reviewers.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — replace the hard-coded tool constants with simple discovery: use `shutil.which()` first for each tool, falling back to the current absolute path only if found there. If neither exists, mark unavailable as today.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_bandit()` treats any non-empty stdout that parses as JSON but lacks a `"results"` key as zero findings, with no failure signal. `_run_tool()` encodes timeouts as `stderr="TIMEOUT"` and nonzero return codes are otherwise ignored. Bandit commonly emits errors in stderr or malformed/partial output on execution problems; this function only raises on `"NOT_FOUND"`. Evidence: `data = json.loads(result.stdout) if result.stdout.strip() else {}` then `for issue in data.get("results", [])`; no check of `returncode`, no timeout handling beyond parse fallback.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can misclassify a broken Bandit invocation as “0 new security issues”, biasing verdicts toward SAFE/NEUTRAL. Health scan also underreports security findings without exposing tool failure, producing misleading whole-body health metrics.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat `stderr == "TIMEOUT"` or any nonzero return code with missing/invalid JSON results as tool failure, not zero findings; log it and surface unavailability/failure consistently as with missing binaries.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` can emit duplicate `context_growth` signals for unrelated causes in the same round: one from total context budget pressure (Check 2) and another from oversized model response (Check 4, which also currently uses `signal_type="context_growth"`). Even if C0041 renames Check 4’s type, the current implementation conflates two separate mechanisms under one bucket. Evidence: both append `PacingSignal(... signal_type="context_growth" ...)` with different `detail`, thresholds, and semantics.
FOLLOW: Consumers that count or branch on signal type can mis-handle response-size anomalies as overall context-budget exhaustion, leading the insect brain to choose the wrong mitigation path or overcount one kind of issue while missing the other. This is especially problematic because pacing signals are meant to guide round control mechanically.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — keep the existing C0041 fix: emit a distinct signal type for Check 4 (`response_size_anomaly`) so each pacing mechanism is separately machine-actionable.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — The documented “defect detection” capability lists categories including `race_condition`, but no current runner can realistically produce evidence for that category in this module’s toolchain. `_categorise_ruff()` maps race/concurrent/thread/lock keywords from message text, but Ruff diagnostics generally do not report concurrency-analysis findings; pyright/mypy categorisers also never emit `RACE_CONDITION`; bandit is forced to `SECURITY`. So the category exists in API surface but is effectively dead for the configured tools. Evidence: only `_categorise_ruff()` contains race-condition keyword logic; no analyzer in `scan_health()` performs concurrency analysis.
FOLLOW: Reviewers and downstream code may assume race-condition monitoring is active when it never fires, overstating feature coverage of the endocrine layer. Given the module is presented as a whole-body monitor, dead advertised categories are misleading outputs rather than harmless polish.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove `race_condition` from the documented supported defect categories in this module until a tool that can actually emit it is wired in; keep the constant if needed for future expansion.
VERIFIED: TRUE
